title: The Early Church Wasn’t Comfortable
paragraphs:
Doors weren’t locked to keep comfort in—
they were locked because death could walk in at any moment.

Not the version of you that treats God like a weekend option.
Not the version of you that scrolls past conviction.
Because the early Church didn’t follow Jesus for blessings.
They followed Him knowing it could cost them everything.

A dimly lit room.
Whispers instead of songs.
Footsteps outside that could mean soldiers.

A mother clutching her child.
A man who already lost his brother to execution.
Because they had seen something you keep avoiding.
They had seen the risen Christ.
“But here’s what most people don’t realize…”
The early Church wasn’t strong because they were fearless.
They were strong because they were transformed.
You say you believe in Jesus.
You still live in hidden sin.
Still justify what God already exposed.
Still delay repentance like tomorrow is guaranteed.
The early believers didn’t play with sin.
Because they understood something terrifying and holy:
“The wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
“…but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”
That’s why they sang in prisons.
That’s why they didn’t run when persecution came.
You want the power of the early Church?
Then you must face what they faced.
You’re not struggling because life is hard.
You’re struggling because your faith is shallow.
And comfort will never save you.
Jesus didn’t die to make you comfortable.
He died to make you clean.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
The early Church didn’t gather because life was easy.
They gathered because they had been forgiven.
Purchased by the blood of Jesus.
And that same invitation stands in front of you.
Drop the sin you keep defending.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
You don’t need a more comfortable life.
Will you keep playing safe Christianity…
Or will you step into the real thing?
If this convicted you, don’t ignore it.
